name: Treaty with the Kickapoo, 1820
aka: Supplementary treaty of St. Louis, July 19, 1820
nations: Kickapoo (Kiikaapoa), today the Kickapoo Tribe in Kansas, the Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma and the Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas
promises: Article 6 of the Edwardsville treaty of July 30, 1819 was rewritten (Article 1).

In exchange for the Illinois cession of 1819, the United States ceded to the Kickapoo a tract in Missouri between the Pomme de Terre and Osage rivers and the Osage line, to be possessed as they had possessed their Illinois lands (amended Article 6).
The United States paid $3,000 in merchandise on the day of signing (amended Article 6).
landTaken: None by this treaty. Royce Area 179 is the Missouri tract this treaty granted to the Kickapoo; Royce records that it was ceded back to the United States by the treaty of October 24, 1832.
compensation: Not applicable to this treaty. For the 1832 cession of the tract, which the Commission recorded as 1,868,500 acres, the Kickapoo claimed an unconscionable price in Docket 193; the claim was settled by compromise for $540,000, entered as final judgment on February 29, 1968.
today: No court or Commission finding that a promise of this treaty was not kept was found. The 1968 compromise concerns the later 1832 treaty.

nationVoice.summary: Chairman Lester Randall told the Senate in 2018 that the United States moved the Tribe from Wisconsin through Illinois and Missouri to Kansas under nine treaties made between 1809 and 1862.
In testimony to Kansas legislators the Tribe sets out the 1832 treaty under which it moved from the country ceded on the Osage River in Missouri to its present reservation in Kansas.

openQuestions: treaties.json treats this entry as a cession of Royce Area 179 in Missouri. Royce's schedule entry for this treaty describes the tract it granted (the area treaties.json numbers 179) to the Kickapoo and that they ceded it in 1832; the cession itself belongs to the treaty of October 24, 1832 (7 Stat. 391). Not edited.
Whether the Kickapoo were able to occupy the tract undisturbed between 1820 and 1832 was not researched.
No Kickapoo nation account of this treaty was found in this pass.
